recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-5342 unless the Security work group separately reopens the broader modern AuditEvent agent target-profile policy.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 ballot item requested broadening SecurityEvent.participant.reference from Practitioner|Patient|Device to include RelatedPerson, with the applied decision also adding Organization and not adding Group at that time.
initial_application: Commit 8e3bf13ba6 applied the issue in 2015 by changing the AuditEvent spreadsheet type from Reference(Practitioner|Patient|Device) to Reference(Practitioner|Organization|Device|Patient|RelatedPerson). Later source migrations and renames moved that behavior into structuredefinition-AuditEvent.xml.
additional_context: AuditEvent is active in source/fhir.ini and the old AuditEvent.participant element maps to AuditEvent.agent. Later final AuditEvent issues renamed agent.reference to agent.who and broadened allowed actor types, including FHIR-17412, FHIR-32454, and FHIR-49672, so the current target-profile list is intentionally broader than the 2015 ballot list.
reconciliation: No source change was made because source/auditevent/structuredefinition-AuditEvent.xml already lists RelatedPerson and Organization on AuditEvent.agent.who, along with other actor types added by later applied decisions.

related_jiras.note: Renamed AuditEvent.agent.reference to AuditEvent.agent.who and simplified Identifier/Reference handling.
Required AuditEvent.agent.who to recognize Event performer.actor types, explaining later expansion beyond the DSTU1 actor list.
Applied R6 Security decision to add newer agent kinds such as HealthcareService to AuditEvent.agent.who.
Workflow actor guidance that informed FHIR-49672 and explains modern Group/HealthcareService actor handling.
